analyst_view.overall: Frosinone (7th, 20 points) host Parma (17th, 8 points) after both were beaten 5-1 last weekend: Frosinone at Milan, Parma at home to Roma. Parma's coach Alberto Gilardino, who took over from Carlos Cuesta during the season, has a thin squad: striker Romero is out until around January with a shoulder injury, Drobnic (foot) and Valenti are out of the defence, and Diego Carlos (adductor) and Bernabé (thigh) are doubtful, while Ndiaye is back after a one-match ban. None of these absences is in the numbers, which had no team news for this match; for Frosinone, midfielder Grillitsch is out and Terzic doubtful. The numbers already lean heavily on Frosinone's recent form (shots +34%, corners +16% from the last six games), and no referee has been named yet. A weaker Parma attack and a patched-up Parma defence roughly cancel out on goals, so the main move is a small trim on shots.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals (1.9 Frosinone, 1.1 Parma) and already add Frosinone's 16 goals in their last six games. Parma lose their striker Romero until about January, which should cost them a little going forward, but their back line is depleted too (Drobnic and Valenti out, Diego Carlos doubtful) after conceding five to Roma; the two point in opposite directions, so I stay at about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.5 corners, mostly Frosinone's 7.5, and they already add a big +16% for Frosinone's 53 corners in their last six games. Parma, short of defenders and likely to sit deep away from home, will concede plenty, but that is what the numbers already assume, so I stay at about 11.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards and already take some off because both sides have been booked less than usual lately; Troilo is Parma's most-booked player recently and Ndiaye returns from a red-card ban. No referee has been named yet and I found nothing new on temper or stakes the numbers can't see, so I stay at about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 38.2 shots, a very high figure, with +34% already added for Frosinone's 135 shots in their last six games. Parma's own share (12.6) should drop a little without Romero, their main striker, with Lontani and Toure expected to lead the line instead, so I trim mildly to about 37.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.1 shots on target and already add +20% for Frosinone's recent accuracy. Parma will create less without Romero, but a defence missing Drobnic and Valenti (Diego Carlos doubtful) should let Frosinone get more efforts on goal; these roughly balance, so I stay at about 11.1.
